Because we generally recognize revenues from our subscription service over the subscription term, a decrease in new subscriptions or renewals may not be immediately reflected in our operating results.

Subscription revenues. Subscription revenues are primarily comprised of fees that give customers access to the ordered subscription service for both self-hosted offerings and cloud-based subscription offerings, and related standard and enhanced support and updates, if any, to the subscription service during the subscription term. For our cloud-based offerings, we recognize revenue ratably over the subscription term. For self-hosted offerings, a substantial portion of the sales price is recognized upon delivery of the software, which may cause greater variability in our subscription revenues and subscription gross margin. Pricing includes multiple instances, hosting and support services, data backup and disaster recovery services, as well as future updates, when and if available, offered during the subscription term. We typically invoice our customers for subscription fees in annual increments upon execution of the initial contract or subsequent renewal. Our contracts are generally non-cancellable during the subscription term, though a customer can terminate for breach if we materially fail to perform.

hits.text: We generally recognize revenues from customers ratably over the terms of their subscriptions. Net new annual contract value from new subscriptions and expansion contracts entered into during a period can generally be expected to generate revenues for the duration of the subscription term. As a result, a significant portion of the revenues we report in each period are derived from the recognition of deferred revenues relating to subscriptions entered into during previous periods. Consequently, a decrease in new or renewed subscriptions, expansion contracts in any single reporting period will have a limited impact on our revenues for that period, but they will negatively affect our operating results in future periods. Our subscription model also makes it difficult for us to rapidly increase our revenues through additional sales in any period, as revenues from new customers are generally recognized over the applicable subscription term. Also, our ability to adjust our cost structure in the event of a decrease in new or renewed subscriptions may be limited.

As described in Note 2 to the consolidated financial statements, subscription revenues are primarily comprised of subscription fees that give customers access to the ordered subscription service, related support and updates, if any, to the subscribed service during the subscription term. The Company recognizes subscription revenues ratably over the contract term beginning on the commencement date of each contract, which is the date the Company makes their services available to their customers. The Company’s contracts with customers typically include a fixed amount of consideration and are generally non-cancellable and without any refund-type provisions. The Company recognized subscription revenues of $10.6 billion for the year ended December 31, 2024.

            entity_type TEXT,
            sic TEXT,
            sic_description TEXT,
            owner_org TEXT,

            name TEXT NOT NULL,

field_guide.cik: Company identifier stored as text. Join filings using both CIK and accession number.
field_guide.fact_name: Raw XBRL concept. Related concepts may have different definitions.
field_guide.fact_category: Taxonomy namespace. Compare concepts only under compatible definitions.
field_guide.fact_value: Value in the returned unit. NULL is missing and never implies zero.
field_guide.unit: Original units. USD values are unscaled dollars.
field_guide.end_date: Fact period end. It can precede the filing's fiscal year.
field_guide.fiscal_year: Fiscal-year label of the disclosure. Verify the fact's actual end_date.
field_guide.fiscal_period: Source fiscal-period label. Check period length and frame for flows.
field_guide.frame: Supplementary period indicator. A missing frame does not establish annual duration.
field_guide.filed_date: Submission date, distinct from the fact period end.
field_guide.form_type: Source filing form. One period may be disclosed in several filings.
field_guide.accession_number: SEC submission identifier. A matching filings row may be absent.
field_guide.dimension_segment: Segment scope if supplied. Absence alone does not prove comparability.
field_guide.dimension_geography: Geographic scope if supplied. Absence alone does not prove comparability.

interpretation_notes: Check end_date, fiscal_period, frame and form_type before comparing flows across periods.
Check concept, unit, period length and dimensions before identifying repeats.
Repeated disclosures can reflect revisions. Retain fact IDs and accession numbers and do not sum repeats.
Do not conflate net income, parent-attributable income, operating income and pretax income.

Renewal rate. We calculate our renewal rate by subtracting our attrition rate from 100%. Our attrition rate for a period is equal to the ACV from customers lost during the period, divided by the sum of (i) the total ACV from all customers that renewed during the period, excluding changes in price or users, and (ii) the total ACV from all customers lost during the period. Accordingly, our renewal rate is calculated based on ACV and is not based on the number of customers that have renewed. Further, our renewal rate does not reflect increased or decreased purchases from our customers to the extent such customers are not lost customers or lapsed renewals. A lost customer is a customer that did not renew an expiring contract and that, in our judgment, will not be renewed. Typically, a customer that reduces its subscription upon renewal is not considered a lost customer. However, in instances where the subscription decrease represents the majority of the customer’s ACV, we may deem the renewal as a lost customer. For our renewal rate calculation, we define a customer as an entity with a separate production instance of our service and an active subscription contract as of the measurement date, instead of an entity with a unique GULT or DUNS number. message.content:
**Answer (ServiceNow, Inc., FY2024 Form 10-K, report period ended December 31, 2024):**

The highlighted subscription-related risk is a **revenue-recognition timing / visibility risk inherent in the subscription business model**: because subscription revenue is recognized ratably over the subscription term, deterioration in new subscriptions or renewals is not immediately visible in reported results.

Direct disclosure (risk-factor bullet, Part I, 2024 10-K):
- "Because we generally recognize revenues from our subscription service over the subscription term, a decrease in new subscriptions or renewals may not be immediately reflected in our operating results." (chunk 1373715/now-20241231:59304 and :117852)

The accompanying risk-factor discussion elaborates the mechanism (chunk 1373715/now-20241231:118053):
- A significant portion of each period's reported revenue comes from recognition of deferred revenue relating to subscriptions entered into in prior periods.
- Therefore a decrease in new or renewed subscriptions or expansion contracts in any single period "will have a limited impact on our revenues for that period, but they will negatively affect our operating results in future periods" — i.e., the shortfall is deferred/lagged rather than visible immediately.
- The model also makes it "difficult for us to rapidly increase our revenues through additional sales in any period," since new-customer revenue is recognized over the applicable subscription term.
- Management adds that "our ability to adjust our cost structure in the event of a decrease in new or renewed subscriptions may be limited," creating a margin/operating-leverage risk.

A related reporting-basis point from the revenue recognition policy (chunk 1373715/now-20241231:173605): for cloud-based offerings revenue is recognized ratably over the subscription term, whereas for self-hosted offerings "a substantial portion of the sales price is recognized upon delivery of the software, which may cause greater variability in our subscription revenues and subscription gross margin." This is a mix-driven variability risk rather than a pure timing risk.

Context: subscription revenue was $10.6 billion for the year ended December 31, 2024 (chunk 1373715/now-20241231:216908), and contracts are generally non-cancellable with fixed consideration, which partly mitigates but does not eliminate the timing risk described above.

Note: these are forward-looking risk-factor statements and accounting-policy descriptions, not evidence that any such decline has actually occurred.
